gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-pilcrow-r: Spacey and stretched out, Alien Encounters floats its letters apart, while Pilcrow Rounded packs its warm, tall-lowercase sans tight with curves left open. Spread against huddled.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-quicksand: Quicksand has lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs. Alien Encounters hovers above it with a far-off, technological air, and the body text can be sized up without hairlines going thin.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-amulya: Modern in a way that feels drawn with a compass, Arkhip keeps one stroke width through every letter and floats them apart. And Amulya, a plain sans, simply leaves generous gaps in its curves for the text.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-chillax: Arkhip's letters float well apart, each with a c open like a bent paperclip. Chillax loosens things further, its spaghetti-like line and unfinished loops making the geometric heading look more buttoned-up.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-spline-sans: Contemporary and friendly, Arkhip spaces its letters far apart and never thickens or thins a stroke. And Spline Sans, a plain sans, matches that with wide gaps where its curves meet the stems.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-synonym: Dependable is the word for Synonym, a sans-serif that lays down a constant stripe of ink, while Arkhip floats its geometric letters well apart. They look like siblings.
gen-dafont-arkhip-outfit: Arkhip floats its modern, geometric letters well apart, with no thick-and-thin modulation anywhere in the alphabet. Outfit, a plain sans, bends its cable-like strokes into curves that stop short of closing, so long paragraphs keep moving.
gen-dafont-arkhip-plus-jakarta-sans: Precise and monoline, Plus Jakarta Sans keeps its curve endings well apart, giving text a modern, orderly texture. Arkhip, shrunk down, would lose its floating letters, whereas this plain sans holds up when enlarged.
gen-dafont-arkhip-space-grotesk: Arkhip scatters its letters wide apart. Space Grotesk, a plain sans, forms each glyph from a ribbon of constant width with counters that breathe, so the geometric heading and body feel like relatives with different tempos.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-nunito: Azonix has capitals barely taller than lowercase, so words need a moment to knit back together. Nunito softens that with big round bowls and terminals clear of the stem, making paragraphs feel friendly and unhurried.
